11                Emily, at the front of the chambers,

13   guest.  

14                Emily was named the New York State 

15   Dairy Princess on February 17th.  A resident of 

16   the village of Valatie, Emily has been serving as 

17   the Columbia County Dairy Princess since 2015.  

18                She was selected for this honor from 

19   two dozen county dairy princesses across New York 

20   State.  Competition in the 53th State Pageant was 

21   rigorous.  Judges evaluated contestants based on

23   dairy industry, poise and personality.  From all

 4                "WHEREAS, Members of the United 

 5   States Armed Forces, who have served so

25   Representative Sean Patrick Maloney presented

 8   second of four children born to his parents; and

10   proudly served his country as a member of the 

11   United States Army from July 8, 1952, until April

13   Third Korean Winter and the Korea Summer of 1953

17   military service, this esteemed veteran married 

18   Clare Farace on May 4, 1957, and together they

22   grandchildren and six great-grandchildren;

16                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

17   Resolution Number 6097, by Senator Serino, 

18   memorializing Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to 

19   proclaim June 2016 as Alzheimer's and Brain 

20   Awareness Month in the State of New York.

21                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   Senator 

22   Serino.

23                SENATOR SERINO:   Thank you, 

24   Mr. President.

25                I thank my colleagues for the 


                                                                3972

 1   opportunity to recognize June as Alzheimer's and 

 2   Brain Awareness Month here in the State of 

 3   New York.

 4                According to the Alzheimer's 

 5   Association, every 66 seconds someone in the 

 6   United States develops Alzheimer's disease, a 

 7   truly debilitating illness that slowly robs 

 8   patients of their most valuable possession, their 

 9   memory.

10                Currently there's no robust 

11   treatment or cure for Alzheimer's and dementia, 

12   and the disease is ultimately fatal, claiming the  

13   lives of nearly one in every three seniors each 

14   and every day.

15                Take a minute to imagine waking up 

16   and not recognizing the faces of the people that 

17   you love most -- not knowing your children, your 

18   spouse, or your best friend.  Devastating is an 

19   understatement.  Alzheimer's is a diagnosis that 

20   affects not only patients but an entire family, 

21   changing life as they knew it forever.

22                This month is about shining a light 

23   on the disease and showing support for those 

24   battling this diagnosis and their families.  And 

25   this resolution is inherently tied to my 


                                                                3973

 1   resolution on World Elder Abuse Awareness Day, 

 2   because those suffering from Alzheimer's and 

 3   dementia are particularly vulnerable to abuse.  

 4                This chamber has recently made an 

 5   unprecedented commitment to combat this 

 6   debilitating disease, having dedicated over 

 7   $25 million to the cause in last year's budget.  

 8   We're making incredible strides, but there is 

 9   still work to be done, which is why pausing to 

10   raise awareness for this disease couldn't be more 

11   important.  

12                I thank you for the opportunity, and 

13   I invite my colleagues to help further the cause 

14   by cosponsoring this resolution and spreading the 

15   word in their home districts.  

16                Thank you, Mr. President.

15                I have to tell you, before becoming 

16   the Aging chair, like so many in our communities, 

17   I had no idea just how serious the elder abuse 

18   epidemic truly is.  The thought of anyone taking 

19   advantage of --

 1                Senator Serino.

 2                SENATOR SERINO:   Thank you, 

 3   Mr. President.

 4                The thought of anyone taking 

 5   advantage of our seniors, the people who have 

 6   spent their lives building and shaping the 

 7   communities that we know and love, is hard to 

 8   fathom.  But the fact is it happens all the time, 

 9   and all too often it happens at the hands of 

10   people our seniors know and trust the most.

11                Last week our Mediation Center held 

12   a daylong conference on the topic, and it will 

13   forever amaze me to hear the statistics on this 

14   issue.  Nearly 5 million cases of elder abuse 

15   occur each year in the United States, but it's 

16   estimated that 85 percent of these incidents go 

17   unreported.  Financial abuse alone costs older 

18   Americans over $2.6 billion each and every year.  

19   And our available data on elder abuse suggests 

20   that only around 1 in 14 incidents come to the 

21   attention of authorities.

22                This day is about raising awareness.  

23   And as you've heard me say, time and time again, 

24   awareness works.  This house has done incredible 

25   work this year to bring elder abuse out of the 


                                                                3976

 1   shadows and to make our seniors' safety a 

 2   priority.  And I thank my colleagues for 

 3   recognizing the importance of this issue.

 4                Our seniors play an invaluable role 

 5   in the fabric of our society, and we have a 

 6   responsibility to ensure that they can live out 

 7   their lives and enjoy the communities they have 

 8   built free from harm and safe from abuse.

 9                Thank you, Mr. President.

13   Mr. President, I rise to commend Senator Serino 

14   on this resolution for elder abuse.  It's an 

15   abuse that is not talked about, and it's an 

16   abuse that affects everyone.  

17                And when people think about elder 

18   abuse, they think of it as someone who's abusing 

19   someone outside of the family.  But 80 percent of 

20   the time it's a family member who's abusing the 

21   elder.  And no one should have to work all their 

22   life to be abused by a family member.

23                And many times a family member who's 

24   elderly gets dementia, and a lot of times we 

25   don't recognize dementia in those, and they get

 1   sick.  And I always say make sure you create a 

 2   will, to make sure the people you want to get

14                So I just want to thank Senator

16   Thank you.  And God bless our seniors.
